problem.claim: Sampling compositional and discrete objects from an unnormalized posterior distribution.

gap.claim: The authors state that Markovian samplers can hamper training signal propagation and catastrophically reduce expressivity through state aliasing.

contributions.claim: Proposes lifting a deterministic MDP with learnable latent dynamics so the policy can depend on the entire past trajectory.
Introduces the resulting approach as path-dependent discrete amortized inference.
Provably extends existing learning algorithms for amortized samplers to the proposed setting.

stated_novelty.claim: The stated distinction is replacing current-state-only Markovian dependence with learnable trajectory-dependent latent dynamics, together with an extension of existing amortized-sampler algorithms.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, on standard benchmark problems, the approach often achieves faster learning convergence than prior techniques.
The authors report improved state-space exploration relative to prior techniques on those benchmarks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frames sampling compositional and discrete objects from an unnormalized posterior.
Describes prior approaches that learn deterministic MDPs progressively building objects in proportion to the posterior.
Argues that the Markovian assumption can impair signal propagation and sampler expressivity through state aliasing.
Introduces trajectory-dependent latent dynamics, extends amortized-sampler algorithms, and reports faster convergence and improved exploration on standard benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a specific modeling assumption—dependence only on the current state—to two distinct failure modes, then matches the proposal to both by using full-trajectory dependence.

lessons.interpretation: A strong abstract can make a method feel motivated by pairing each identified limitation with an explicit design change.
lessons.application: When presenting a new architecture, map each claimed failure mode to the mechanism intended to address it, while preserving the claim's scope.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the abstract lacks evidence or when the proposed mechanism is not clearly connected to the stated limitation.

unknowns: The abstract provides no quantitative benchmark results, convergence definitions, exploration metrics, or details about the standard problems and prior techniques.
The scope of “often” and the conditions of the reported improvements are unspecified.
